# 3rd-Party Backup Integrations — Veeam, Commvault, Veritas NetBackup, Rubrik, Cohesity

## Veeam
- [Veeam & NetApp configuration guide and best practices (Veeam wp)](https://www.veeam.com/resources/wp-netapp-configuration-and-best-practices-guide-for-veeam-backup.html)
- [Adding NetApp ONTAP — Veeam Backup & Replication user guide](https://helpcenter.veeam.com/docs/vbr/userguide/netapp_add.html)
- [Adding NetApp ONTAP — Storage System Snapshot Integration Guide](https://helpcenter.veeam.com/docs/backup/storage/netapp_add.html)
- [Veeam Backup & Replication 12.3 — NetApp ONTAP SnapDiff API enabled (Veeam community)](https://community.veeam.com/blogs-and-podcasts-57/veeam-backup-and-replication-12-3-now-has-netapp-ontap-snapdiff-api-enabled-9312)
- Mechanism: Veeam's Snapshot Orchestration creates a primary ONTAP snapshot, updates SnapVault/SnapMirror secondaries, then backs up changed-block data — no separate backup-to-repository step required for the snapshot tier.
- NAS/SMB share backup uses native storage integration plus **SnapDiff** to identify changed files since the last backup without a filesystem crawl — significantly reduces NAS backup windows.
- **Update 2026-07-05**: **VBR 12.3** adds native **SnapDiff API**-based Changed File Tracking (CFT) — this is ONTAP's own differencing engine surfaced directly to Veeam (v1 of this integration, more capability expected in future releases), further reducing NAS backup windows versus the prior SnapDiff-assisted crawl approach. Caveats: CFT is **not** supported on ONTAP 9.10.1 through 9.10.1P10, and **not** supported for **FlexGroup volumes** — confirm the target ONTAP version/volume type before relying on CFT rather than the older SnapDiff path. Veeam's own QA has separately validated **ONTAP 9.16.1 GA** as supported in its storage integration guide — always cross-check Veeam's published ONTAP support matrix against the customer's actual ONTAP version, since Veeam's qualification lags NetApp's own release cadence.
- Best practice: cap Snapshot Orchestration retry count at ≤3 (or disable auto-retry) to avoid runaway snapshot accumulation on repeated job failures.

This indicates the previously-flagged VM-backup gap for NetApp has closed. ## Commvault
- [NetApp best practices — Commvault documentation](https://documentation.commvault.com/saas/best_practices_for_netapp_storage_array.html)
- [Commvault supported technologies: NetApp](https://www.commvault.com/supported-technologies/netapp)
- Mechanism: IntelliSnap integration drives ONTAP snapshot-based protection and recovery.
- Best practice: point NAS client/storage array configuration at a data LIF (e.g., e0a/e0b), never the management LIF (e0M); disable ONTAP-native snapshot schedules on any volume managed by Commvault to avoid retention/policy conflicts; use two backupsets to run snapshot and backup-to-tape operations in parallel against the same data.

### Commvault Flex with NetApp (new, found and direct-fetch confirmed 2026-08-17)
- **Re-checked 2026-10-08, direct fetch**: the press release still reads "targeted for general availability this summer." No GA announcement found. Now more than a month past the end of northern summer. Do not position Commvault Flex with NetApp as available without a current Commvault confirmation.

No version or GA date given. This is a separate item from Commvault Flex.
- [Commvault Expands Commvault Flex to Hitachi Vantara and NetApp for Scalable Resilience in the AI Era (press release, 2026-04-15)](https://ir.commvault.com/news-releases/news-release-details/commvault-expands-commvault-flex-hitachi-vantara-and-netapp) — separate from the Metallic/IntelliSnap integration above and from the March 2026 ARP/Synthetic Recovery alliance ([Advanced vendor capabilities](#advanced-vendor-capabilities-2026) below). **Commvault Flex** (formerly HyperScale Flex) is a software-image data-protection appliance architecture that connects to external high-performance flash storage pools rather than internal disk; this announcement extends the Flex partner ecosystem (previously Everpure, HPE, VAST Data) to add **NetApp and Hitachi Vantara** as qualified storage partners, letting a customer run Commvault Flex against NetApp flash storage for petabyte-scale AI-dataset protection/recovery.

Treat this as an overdue/stalled roadmap item, not just "still on track": flag explicitly to a customer that the announced timeline has passed without a public GA confirmation, and verify current status directly with Commvault/NetApp account teams before scoping a design around Commvault Flex on NetApp storage.
- **Re-confirmed 2026-09-14, direct-fetch of the press release itself**: page text is byte-for-byte the same as the prior checks — still *"targeted for general availability this summer,"* no GA update appended, no separate GA announcement found. ## Veritas NetBackup
- [NDMP support for clustered Data ONTAP — NetBackup for NDMP admin guide](https://www.veritas.com/support/en_US/doc/24427212-131831692-0/v108973812-131831692)
- [Prepare ONTAP NDMP configurations](https://docs.netapp.com/us-en/ontap/ndmp/prepare-ndmp-config-task.html)
- TR-4879 — NetApp converged infrastructure data protection (covers NetBackup integration patterns)
- Best practice: run the cDOT cluster in SVM-scoped (Vserver-aware) NDMP mode rather than node-scoped — enables the CAB extension for optimal backup/restore/duplication of FlexVol volumes; provision at least one intercluster LIF per node that doesn't already host a cluster-management LIF.

## Rubrik
- Mechanism: Rubrik triggers ONTAP snapshots via NetApp APIs and was the first backup vendor granted access to the **SnapDiff API**, which lets Rubrik enumerate changed data for cloud archival in seconds/minutes instead of hours.

## Cohesity
- [Configure and register NetApp ONTAP — Cohesity DataProtect docs](https://docs.cohesity.com/baas/data-protect/configure-register-netapp.htm)
- [What NAS protocols does Cohesity support for ONTAP? (KB)](https://kb.netapp.com/on-prem/ontap/da/NAS/NAS-KBs/What_NAS_Protocols_does_Cohesity_support_for_ONTAP)
- Supported protocols: NFS and CIFS/SMB registration and backup of ONTAP clusters/SVMs via Cohesity DataProtect/Cloud Protection Service.
- **Cohesity DataHawk retired as a standalone product — new, direct-fetch confirmed 2026-09-07**: [Cohesity DataHawk updates blog](https://www.cohesity.com/blogs/cohesity-datahawk-updates-what-you-need-to-know/) (article dated 2026-05-21 per page metadata, banner added after original 2024 publication) now carries a standing notice, quoted directly: *"We have retired Cohesity DataHawk as a separate product... making all our capabilities for detection, investigation, response, and recovery automation part of Cohesity Data Cloud Enterprise Edition."* This means the "DataHawk" product name is deprecated — its threat-protection, data-classification/DSPM, and cyber-vaulting (FortKnox) capabilities now ship as part of **Cohesity Data Cloud Enterprise Edition** rather than a separately branded/licensed module. **Practical effect for a customer conversation**: don't scope or quote "Cohesity DataHawk" as a distinct SKU going forward — confirm current Enterprise Edition packaging/entitlement with Cohesity before referencing this capability set by name. See the [Advanced vendor capabilities](#advanced-vendor-capabilities-2026) DataHawk entry below, retained for historical/technical accuracy of what the capability set does, but the product-naming/packaging details there are now superseded by this note. **Re-confirmed 2026-09-14, direct-fetch**: the same retirement banner is still live on the page verbatim (article `modified_time` metadata unchanged at 2026-05-21) — no reversal, no change.

## HYCU
**New section, added 2026-07-11** — not previously indexed in this library despite being an active, named NetApp ONTAP backup partner.
- [HYCU for NetApp ONTAP — solution page](https://www.hycu.com/solutions/data-protection/netapp-ontap) · [HYCU R-Cloud platform — new features/innovations](https://www.hycu.com/new)
- Mechanism: **agentless** — no agent to install/update on the ONTAP cluster or protected workloads; integrates via **native REST API** calls against ONTAP rather than an installed collector/proxy footprint. Positions itself as a lighter-weight alternative to the agent- or appliance-based integration models used by Veeam/Commvault/Cohesity/Rubrik above.
- **HYCU R-Shield**: extends malware/threat hunting to ONTAP file workloads specifically — scans data using **YARA rules** (a pattern-matching signature format widely used in malware research) without impacting production I/O or the backup job itself. This is a DSPM/threat-detection-adjacent capability layered on backup data, the same architectural pattern already documented for Cohesity DataHawk and Rubrik Security Cloud in [Advanced vendor capabilities](#advanced-vendor-capabilities-2026) below — cross-reference [DSPM](../DSPM/README.md) when a customer is evaluating HYCU specifically for its security/scanning angle rather than pure backup/restore.
- **Positioning note**: worth surfacing alongside Veeam/Commvault/Cohesity/Rubrik/Veritas when a customer's evaluation criteria explicitly weight agentless deployment and operational simplicity over the deeper native-integration surface (e.g., Rubrik's SnapDiff API first-mover access, Veeam's SnapDiff-based CFT) that the incumbent vendors above have built up over a longer integration history — confirm HYCU's current NetApp-specific feature parity (snapshot orchestration depth, NAS SnapDiff support) against the customer's specific requirements before treating it as a drop-in equivalent.

## Cross-vendor operational note
- For every third-party backup product above, the recurring failure mode is **schedule collision**: the backup vendor's own snapshot/retention schedule and an independently configured ONTAP-native Snapshot policy both firing against the same volume, exhausting the Snapshot count ceiling or producing inconsistent RPOs. Standard remediation: disable the ONTAP-native schedule on any volume placed under third-party snapshot orchestration and let the backup product own the schedule end-to-end.

## Advanced vendor capabilities (2026)
Each of the major backup vendors has extended beyond "back up and restore" into cloud-native and cyber-resilience/DSPM-adjacent territory. This matters when scoping a modern data-protection architecture, not just a backup job.

- **Commvault Metallic (DMaaS)** — [Commvault supported technologies: NetApp](https://www.commvault.com/supported-technologies/netapp) / [NetApp Data Protection in Metallic docs](https://documentation.metallic.io/2024e/essential/netapp_data_protection.html) / [Backup and recover using StorageGRID and Commvault](https://docs.netapp.com/us-en/storagegrid-enable/technical-reports/commvault-index.html). Metallic is Commvault's SaaS Data-Management-as-a-Service layer; it natively integrates with **Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP** and **Azure NetApp Files**, extending the on-prem IntelliSnap integration ([base capability](#commvault)) into a cloud-delivered control plane covering AWS/Azure/GCP/Oracle Cloud. NetApp Scale-out Data Protection (SDP) reference architecture combines NetApp HCI/AFF/StorageGRID with Commvault for on-prem object-storage-backed protection at scale — relevant when a customer wants on-prem economics with cloud-DMaaS management.
- **NetApp–Commvault strategic alliance / Closed-Loop Recovery Architecture (new, announced 2026-03-24)** — [NetApp and Commvault Advance Cyber Resilience with Strategic Alliance (Commvault news)](https://www.commvault.com/news/netapp-and-commvault-advance-cyber-resilience-with-strategic-alliance). Goes beyond the existing Metallic/IntelliSnap integrations: combines NetApp's AI-powered **Autonomous Ransomware Protection (ARP/AI)** on primary storage with Commvault's threat-aware backup and Synthetic Recovery, so an ARP detection signal on primary storage feeds directly into an automated, validated Commvault recovery workflow (early-detection-to-validated-recovery, not just snapshot-triggered backup). Roadmap item flagged in the announcement: future joint work to use **NetApp ONTAP restore technology as the recovery target itself**, aiming to shrink data loss and recovery time further. Treat this as directionally announced/roadmap-stage as of this check — confirm current productization status before scoping a customer design around the closed-loop pattern specifically (the base Metallic/IntelliSnap integration above is separately and currently GA).
- **Veritas Alta Data Protection** — [Veritas Alta Data Protection overview (WWT)](https://www.wwt.com/blog/veritas-alta-data-protection-powered-by-cloud-scale-technology) / [Veritas Alta Data Protection datasheet (PDF)](https://www.veritas.com/content/dam/www/en_us/documents/data-sheet/DS_veritas_alta_data_protection_V1807.pdf). Alta is the cloud-native, "Cloud Scale Technology"-powered evolution of NetBackup — same underlying SnapDiff-accelerated NetApp integration ([base capability](#veritas-netbackup)) but delivered as a scalable, cloud/hybrid-multi-cloud data-protection service rather than an on-prem media-server deployment. Relevant for customers consolidating NetBackup estate into a SaaS-operated model without giving up the NetApp SnapDiff acceleration path.
- **Cohesity DataHawk** — [DataHawk platform](https://www.cohesity.com/platform/datahawk/) / [DataHawk solution brief (PDF)](https://www.cohesity.com/content/dam/cohesity/resource-assets/solution-brief/datahawk-solution-brief-en.pdf). Bundles three capabilities on top of base Cohesity DataProtect ([base capability](#cohesity)): AI/ML-driven **threat protection** (malware/ransomware behavioral scanning, including third-party scan-engine partnerships such as Sophos, announced at RSAC 2026), **ML-based data classification** (the DSPM-adjacent piece — see [DSPM](../DSPM/README.md)), and **cyber vaulting** (FortKnox, an isolated/air-gapped recovery vault). DataHawk explicitly supports scanning NetApp NAS shares and NetApp VMs, not just Cohesity-native storage. Cohesity has also begun integrating third-party DSPM platforms (e.g., Normalyze) directly into DataHawk rather than building 100% in-house classification.
- **Rubrik Security Cloud / Rubrik DSPM** — [Rubrik DSPM product page](https://www.rubrik.com/products/data-security-posture-management) / [Rubrik NAS Cloud Direct for NetApp (PDF)](https://www.rubrik.com/content/dam/rubrik/en/resources/solutions-brief/rubrik-nas-cloud-direct-for-netapp.pdf). Beyond the base SnapDiff-driven snapshot integration ([base capability](#rubrik)), Rubrik NAS Cloud Direct adds native Data ONTAP API-level integration for system discovery, snapshot coordination, and file-permission preservation, and Rubrik Security Cloud layers DSPM (sensitive-data discovery/classification/monitoring) plus Data Detection and Response (DDR — anomalous-access-pattern alerting) on top, managed from a single pane across on-prem/cloud/SaaS.

**Related — NetApp–Elastio partnership (2026-03-24, newly documented this refresh)**: announced the same day as the Commvault alliance above, embeds Elastio Provable Recovery Control (deep snapshot-content inspection for zero-day/staged/stealth threats) into the NetApp Ransomware Resilience managed service — see [Security-Hardening — Ransomware protection](../Security-Hardening/README.md#ransomware-protection) for detail. Roadmap-stage, planned to start with Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP.

**Cross-cutting point for solution design:** all four vendors are converging on the same pattern — backup platform as the substrate, with a DSPM/threat-detection layer bolted on top (either native or via a named third-party DSPM partner). None of these replace ONTAP's own [Autonomous Ransomware Protection](../Security-Hardening/README.md#ransomware-protection) — they operate at the backup-copy/index level (scanning backup data, or monitoring access patterns via API/FPolicy-like hooks) whereas ARP operates in-line on live production I/O. The two layers are complementary, not redundant: ARP catches an in-progress attack on live data fastest; the backup-vendor DSPM/threat-detection layer adds a second detection point against the backup copies themselves and is useful for validating that a restore point predates the compromise.
